packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind as to the manuscript fragment; no identification of the fragment's text was revealed to me by prior context)

EXPOSURE NOTE
The overview image-001 necessarily shows part of the HOST volume: a printed
title page in Italian (partly visible words: "DEI C..", "SCRIT..", "DI GIVLIO",
"Infiniti luoghi dell..", "de gli Euan..", "IN VENE..", "Appresso Barezz..")
and a handwritten ownership-type note on the facing leaf. This concerns the
printed book in whose gutter the manuscript strips sit, not the manuscript
text itself; I did not use it for reading the strips and draw no inference
from it.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only) - from image-001 (overview) and image-002 (first tile)
image-001: an opened printed book; in the gutter, beside a paper mm/cm scale
(0-19 cm), a narrow strip (or series of strips) of written parchment is
visible as a sewing guard / spine-lining stub (tentative interpretation of
function), only c. 8-12 mm of width exposed. The strip is interrupted by the
sewing stations (cords with thread at c. 0.5-1.5 cm, 4 cm, 9 cm, 15 cm, 18.5
cm); written sections are visible at c. 0-3.7 cm, 5-8.7 cm, 10-14.2 cm and
15.8-18 cm. Text lines run horizontally (perpendicular to the gutter), so each
visible "line" is a slice of 3-8 letters from the middle or edge of a line of
a gothic book hand in dark brown ink. No rubric, initial, running title or
gloss can be seen in the overview. Column structure cannot be observed: the
exposure is far narrower than a column.

TRANSCRIPTION (each line is a fragment a few letters wide; "]" and "[" mark that text continues hidden on both sides)

image-002 (native tile, scale 0 to c. 2.9 cm; top section, crossed by sewing thread at c. 1.2-1.8 cm)
image-002 line 1: ]...m(?)i(?)[      (at c. 0.2 cm; only feet of minims, abraded)
image-002 line 2: ]q(ui)? p(?)a(?) n(?)[      (c. 0.7 cm: a "q" or "p" with descender and superscript mark, a small group with superscript "a"-like sign, then a tall letter at the right edge)
image-002 line 3: ]p(?) .. e(?)[      (c. 1.0 cm: "p"/"d"-like letter, then broken traces; partly under thread)
image-002 line 4: ]ale(?) / ]de(?) ...ti(?)o(?)[      (c. 1.7 cm: under the thread; tall letter + "e", then letters at right edge)
image-002 line 5: ]missis(?) / ]uillis(?) n(?)o[      (c. 2.0 cm: minims, then two tall letters "ll"/"ss"/"ſſ" with an abbreviation stroke above, "i", final "s"; then a dark group at the right edge)
image-002 line 6: ]a(?) se(?) / ]aſe c(?)[ ...      (c. 2.3 cm: "a", long-s, "e"; then "c"/"e" and faded letters)
image-002 line 7: ]ab(?)it(?) / ]abir(?) co[      (c. 2.5 cm: "a"?, "b", minim(s), "t"/"r"; then "co"/"ce" at the edge)
image-002 line 8: ]..p(?)..t(?)[      (c. 2.8 cm: badly rubbed, lower edge of the section)

image-003 (native tile, c. 2.6 to 7.5 cm; OVERLAPS image-002 at its top: image-003 lines 1-2 = image-002 lines 7-8)
image-003 line 1: ]...co[      (= image-002 line 7, only the right end, at top edge)
image-003 line 2: ]..p(?)c(?)in(?)[      (= image-002 line 8; "r"/"p" + rubbed letters)
[gap: dark opening at sewing station, c. 3.7-4.9 cm, no parchment]
image-003 line 3: ]o(?)d(?)ul(?) ab[ / ]...nil ab[      (c. 5.3 cm: rubbed; a round letter, "d"?, minims with an abbreviation stroke, tall letter, then "ab"/"ali")
image-003 line 4: ]mitte(?) / ]uitte(?) ca[      (c. 5.8 cm: minims with a tall hooked stroke above, "tte"/"tce", then "ca"/"co")
image-003 line 5: ]ad(?) t(ra)di(?) / ]tal(?) i(n) tali(?)[      (c. 6.2 cm: first group "ad"/"tal"/"cd", then a tall "l"/"i", then a group with tall letters "tradi-"/"tali"/"cali")
image-003 line 6: ]ani(?) / ]arii(?) nece[      (c. 6.6 cm: "a" + minims with a suspension stroke - "an(n)i"/"a(n)i(m)i"/"arii"; then "nece"/"nere"/"nete")
image-003 line 7: ]uo(?) inh(?)[ / ]uo lib(?)[      (c. 7.0 cm: "uo"/"no"; a small superscript sign like "m"/"rꝛ" stands above between the words; then "inh"/"lib"/"mh")
image-003 line 8: ]li(?) qui m(?)[ / ]h q(ui)a m[      (c. 7.4 cm: tall letter + minim, "qui"/"q(ua)m", then minims)
image-003 line 9: [tops of letters only at the bottom edge]

image-004 (native tile, c. 7.0 to 12.3 cm; OVERLAPS image-003 at its top: image-004 lines 1-2 = image-003 lines 7-8)
image-004 line 1: ]uo(?) inh(?)[      (= image-003 line 7, bottoms only)
image-004 line 2: ]li(?) qui(?) in[ / ]h qui m[      (= image-003 line 8, clearer: tall "l"/"h" + minim, "qui", then "m"/"in"/"ui")
image-004 line 3: ]ip(?)iani(?) / ]quam(?) p(?)[ / ]..p..um n[      (c. 7.9 cm: abraded; a "p"/"q" descender near the start, minims with a suspension stroke, then a letter group at right "p"/"n")
image-004 line 4: ]s(?) etatis(?) / ]c a(n)tiq(?)[ / ]e catas(?)[      (c. 8.3 cm: a clear large "a" (or "ct"), then "t", minims/"a", "ti", and a final "s"/"g"/"q"-like letter at the edge; I read "etatis" or "a(n)tiq(u)-" as the two best candidates)
[gap: sewing station with cord, c. 8.7-9.9 cm, no text]
image-004 line 5: ]ie(?) ieiuni[ / ]ic ieiuni[      (c. 10.1 cm: "ie"/"ic"/"re", then "ieiuni"/"ieuin"/"iciuni" - a run of minims with "e"; "ieiuni-" is the reading I prefer but it is a minim-count judgement)
image-004 line 6: ]actu(m)(?) late[ / ]acta lite[      (c. 10.6 cm: "actu" with a stroke above the u, or "acta"; then "late"/"lite"/"lac")
image-004 line 7: ]q(uo)d(?) d(omi)n(u)s(?) e[ / ]q . dn(u)s e[      (c. 11.1 cm: "q" with a mark, "d" with round back, minims + "9"/"s"-like ending under a suspension stroke - "d(omi)n(u)s"/"d(omi)ni"/"dius"; then "e" with a stroke above = "e(st)"/"e(ss)e"/"e(n)-")
image-004 line 8: ]c(?) op(er)is(?) li[ / ]t op(er)ib(?)[      (c. 11.6 cm: "c"/"t", then "op" with crossed descender + "is"/"ib"; then tall letters "li"/"h")
image-004 line 9: [tops only at the bottom edge, c. 12.2 cm]

image-005 (native tile, c. 11.0 to 16.0 cm; OVERLAPS image-004 at its top: image-005 lines 1-2 = image-004 lines 7-8)
image-005 line 1: ]q(?)d(?)...u(?) e[      (= image-004 line 7, lower half only)
image-005 line 2: ]t(?) op(er)is(?) li[ / ]c op(er)ib(us)(?)[      (= image-004 line 8; first letter "t"/"c"/"x", "op" with crossed descender, minim + "s", then tall letters)
image-005 line 3: ]it(?) a(?) d(?)e(?)ui(?) g[ / ]ita diui(?) g[      (c. 12.1 cm: "it"/"ir"/"lt" at the left edge, then a rubbed group with "a", "d"?, minims, and a clear large "g" (or "q"/"o" with tail) at the right edge)
image-005 line 4: ]c(?) adiun(?)... t(?)[ / ]t ad im...[      (c. 12.6 cm: "c"/"t" at the left edge with a tick above, then "ad" + minims, and a horizontal-topped letter "t"/"c" group at the right, rubbed)
image-005 line 5: ]d(?)abit(?) / ]bah(?) / ]dah... ali(?) / do(?)[      (c. 13.1 cm: faded; a "d"/"b" with tall ascender, "a", another tall letter "b"/"h"; then a group at the right "ali"/"dei"/"du")
image-005 line 6: ]t(?)uu(?)m(?)... h(?)[      (c. 13.6 cm: very faded minims; a darker tall letter at the right edge)
image-005 line 7: ]ouit(?) / ]mit(?) / ]B(?)uiti... a(?)n(?)[      (c. 14.1 cm: darker at left - a round bowl letter "o"/"b"/"B" + minims + "t"/"x": "ouit"/"buit"/"mix"; then faded letters "ea"/"sa" and minims at the right edge)
[gap: sewing station with cord, c. 14.3-15.7 cm, no text]
image-005 line 8: ]ic(?) c(?)ip(?)... u(?)[      (c. 15.9 cm: = image-006 line 1, see there)

image-006 (native tile, c. 15.3 to 19 cm; OVERLAPS image-005 at its top: image-006 line 1 = image-005 line 8; bottom section, damaged and covered by loose thread from c. 17.8 cm)
image-006 line 1: ]ic(?) cu(m)(?) p(?) w(?)[ / ]iceip(?)' u[      (c. 15.9 cm: "ic"/"ie", then "c" + minims, a "p" with descender and a superscript hook, then "u"/"w"-like double letter at the edge)
image-006 line 2: ]n(?)a(?) a(n)i(?)e(?) co[ / ]mda ie co[      (c. 16.4 cm: minims, an "a"/"d" with a small superscript "o"-like sign above; "a"/"d" + tall "i"/"l" with a diamond-shaped dot or superscript letter above; "e"/"c"; then "co"/"ca" at the edge. Two superscript marks stand above this line.)
image-006 line 3: ]. m(?)ri(?)... is(?) / ]imi... b(?)[      (c. 16.9 cm: a point, then "m"/"in" + "r"-like letters, rubbed middle, a darker "s"/"b"/"g" at the right edge)
image-006 line 4: ]c(?)e(?)s(?) / ]ib(us)(?) uo(?)... [      (c. 17.3 cm: faded; a rounded group at left, then a tall stroke + "o"/"e" + minims: "uo"/"ho"/"lon")
image-006 line 5: ]t(?)uu(?)i(?) et(?) / ]..um ct[      (c. 17.7 cm: faded minims with a suspension stroke above at the left; a darker "ct"/"et"/"cr" group near the right)
image-006 line 6: [holes and loose thread; traces of one more line at c. 18.1 cm: "...d(?)...e(?)..." illegible]
image-006 below: parchment ends in a frayed edge at c. 18.7 cm; no further text.

SECOND VIEW - image-007 (reduced overview) with its tiles
image-007: another opening of the same kind of volume (no scale in this
view): a blank/offset-stained printed leaf at left, a torn and crumpled
paper leaf (paste-down or endleaf, tentative) at right, and between them in
the gutter a written parchment strip in four sections separated by three
sewing stations (cords visible as brown stubs). Same kind of gothic book hand,
dark brown ink. OBSERVATION: in the second section from the top there is a
small RED mark (looks like a red bracket/paraph or part of a red letter) and
immediately below it a faint greenish/blue trace - the only colour seen in the
packet. Tentative interpretation: this is the other end of the book (or the
other side of the same guard), showing a different slice of the same or a
related leaf; I cannot tell from the images whether it is the reverse of the
strip seen in image-001.

image-008 (native tile: top section of the image-007 strip, under crossing sewing thread; exposure tapers to a few mm)
image-008 line 1: ]u(?) i(?)[      (top, under thread: two dark upright strokes)
image-008 line 2: ]i(?) t(?) b(?)[      (below the thread knot: stroke tops, a darker square letter)
image-008 line 3: ]l(?) n(?) u(?)[ / ]h..n[      (dark upright at left edge, then minims; a thread crosses)
image-008 line 4: ]l(?) .. ſ(?) e(?)[ / ]b . r(?) eo(?)[      (upright at left; a tall "ſ"/"r" form in the middle; rounded letters at the right, rubbed)
image-008 line 5: ]r(?)i(?) .. m(?)[      (faded: an "r"/"t" top, then minims at the right)
image-008 line 6: ]t(?) m(?)i(?) o(?) x(?)[ / ]c in o t[      (dark upright at left edge, faint minims, a round dark blot/letter "o", then a crossed form "x"/"t" at the tear)
image-008 line 7: ]i(?)l(?) ... e(?)t(?)[      (bottom edge of the section: stroke tops and feet only; torn)
(No word can be read with any confidence in this tile.)

image-009 (native tile: bottom of the top section, first sewing station, and most of the second section of the image-007 strip; OVERLAPS image-008 at its top: image-009 line 1 = image-008 line 7)
image-009 line 1: ]i(?) l(?) ... et(?)[      (= image-008 line 7; torn lower edge of top section)
[gap: sewing station with cord stub]
image-009 line 2: ]...l(?) . i(?)[      (top of second section, torn: only feet/tops)
image-009 line 3: ]h(?)[ ... ]i(?)[      (a tall letter "h"/"li" at the left; a hole in the middle; a stroke at the right)
image-009 line 4: ]t(?)... l(?)i(?) ... nc(?) / ne(?)[      (very abraded; darker minims + "c"/"e" at the right edge)
image-009 line 5: ]f(?)/ſ(?) ..ac(?) / ..ue(?) e(?)[ / c(?)[      (a long descending stroke at the left - long s or f; then "ac"/"ue"/"ar"; then a round "e"/"c" with a tail at the right)
image-009 line 6: ]r(?)muni(?) / ]muui(?) / ]inimi(?)[      (a clear run of about seven minims after an "r"/"c"-like first stroke; last stroke slightly separate: "-muni"/"-nimu"/"-inimi"/"-rumii")
image-009 line 7: ]t(?)ioni(?) / ]tom(?) / ]cion[      ("t"/"c" + "i", round "o", minims: "-tioni"/"-cion(em)"/"tom-")
image-009 red: directly below line 7 a RED rectangular frame line (top and left sides of a box, c. 2 lines high) with solid red at the far left edge and red dots inside; below it a GREEN/blue-green horizontal line and a green curved shape at the lower right. Tentative interpretation: the corner of a decorated or framed initial (red frame, green infill or flourishing), cut by the gutter. Within/over the frame, dark letter traces:
image-009 line 8: [inside the red frame] ...l(?) / I(?) ... o(?)[      (a tall dark stroke through the frame; a round letter "o"/"e" at the right)
image-009 line 9: ]i(?)n(?)m(?)... i(?)l(?)[ / ]tur(?) ... h[      (below the green line: faded brown minims; a tall letter beside the green curve)
image-009 line 10: ]..iuuil(?)r(?) / ]..mik(?) / ]..uuli:[      (bottom of tile: minims, then a tall letter with a looped or flagged top like "k"/"lr"/"b")

image-010 (native tile: bottom of the second section, second sewing station, top of the third section; OVERLAPS image-009 at its top: image-010 line 1 = image-009 line 10)
image-010 line 1: ]..um(?)il(?)r(?) / ]..mik(?)[      (= image-009 line 10; green trace above it at upper right)
image-010 line 2: ]..f(?)icau(?) / ]..ticati(?) / ]. ricau(?)[      (faded start with a tall letter; then clear "icau"/"ican"/"icati" - "i", "c", "a", minims; cut at lower edge of section)
[gap: sewing station with cord stub; a dark smudge on the white spine material]
image-010 line 3: ]ni(?)s(?) q(?)/z(?) ..da(?) / ]mis (et)(?) ..[      (top of third section: minims, a round "s"-like letter, a sign like "z"/"q"/tironian et, then letters with an abbreviation stroke above, ending "da"/"ca")
image-010 line 4: ]ualida(?) / ]uili ſa(?) / ]mlsa(?)[      (minims, tall "l", "i", then a tall hooked letter "d"/"ſ" + "a", and a further letter at the edge: "ualida-"/"uilisa"/"milia"?)
image-010 line 5: ]el(?)eao(?) / ]cl(?)ico(?) v(?)[ / ]d(?)icao n[      (tall letter after "e"/"c", then "i/e", "a"/"c", round "o"; then "v"/"n"/"ri" at the right edge)
image-010 line 6: ]uniuerat(?) il[ / ]mmerent(?) il[ / ]uiuerent h[      (a long run of minims with "e" and "r": "uniuer-"/"numer-"/"uiuer-", ending "at"/"ct"/"ent"; then two tall strokes "il"/"ll"/"h" at the right edge)
image-010 line 7: [tops of letters at the bottom edge only]

image-011 (native tile: rest of the third section and the third sewing station of the image-007 strip; OVERLAPS image-010 at its top: image-011 lines 1-2 = image-010 lines 5-6)
image-011 line 1: [= image-010 line 5; feet of letters only at the top edge]
image-011 line 2: ]uniuerat(?) il[ / ]mmerent(?) il[      (= image-010 line 6, complete here: minims, "er"/"cr", "a"/"e", "t"/"n", then "il"/"ll"/"h")
image-011 line 3: ]dob(?)us(?) / ]ib(?) duos(?) / ]sub dio(?) c(?) . ila(?)[      (dark blotted letters: a group with a "b"/"d", then "uis"/"dig"/"dios", a "c"/"e"; then after a point or small gap "ila"/"ua"/"da" at the right edge, the last letters darker)
image-011 line 4: ]il(?) 9(?)/g(?) [hole] o(?) [hole] o(?)[      (two tall strokes at the left; a large looped sign like "9"/"g"/con-abbreviation around a wormhole, from which a long brown diagonal stroke descends to the lower left across the next two lines - a pen flourish, a descender, or a stain, undecided; then round letters beside two more holes)
image-011 line 5: ]u(?)x(?) ... i(?) : [hole][      (abraded; crossed strokes at the left where the diagonal passes; two small dots like a colon/punctus elevatus before a large hole)
image-011 line 6: ]b(?) ..t(?)u(?)l(?)... li(?)[ / ]h. tal.. h[      (dark minims at the left edge, then a darker group in the middle "tal"/"ral"/"cul", tall strokes at the right; much abraded)
image-011 line 7: ]n(?) dom(?)ini(?) b(?) / ]u consulib(?)[ / ]b(?)o nuiulh[      (last line of the section: a dark stroke under the thread at far left, then "do"/"co"/"bo", a run of minims, and tall letters "li"/"ib"/"h" near the right edge; "d(omi)ni"-like minims possible but not safe)
[gap: third sewing station with cord stub; white spine material; then the top edge of the fourth section]

image-012 (native tile: fourth (bottom) section of the image-007 strip; OVERLAPS image-011 only in the blank gap at its top)
Observations: the bottom section is badly wormed, skinned and partly covered by the torn paper leaf at the right and by knotted thread at lower left. Faint pinkish/red stains occur mid-section and near the bottom (possibly offset of red ink; uncertain). In the lowest part the letter-forms that survive are large and clear but appear to be ORIENTED DIFFERENTLY from the sections above (they look inverted or belong to a different, larger script) - observation only.
image-012 line 1: ]l(?) [hole][      (single tall stroke below the top edge, beside a hole)
image-012 line 2: ]...r(?)[      (traces; dark stroke at the right edge of the exposed strip)
image-012 line 3: ]i(?) . i(?)...[      (faded specks only)
image-012 line 4: ]o(?) i(?)l(?) [hole] ... l(?)[      (small hole, then an upright; another hole; upright at the right)
image-012 line 5: ]...s(?) / g(?)[ and below it ]h(?) / b(?)[      (two dark letters at the right edge, one above the other: a round "s"/"g"/"9" and a "b"/"h")
image-012 line 6: ]..c(?)t(?) / L(?)[      (below the loose thread: a short horizontal group ending in an angular "L"/"t" form)
image-012 line 7: ]ll(?)a(?)q(?) p[ / as seen: "ııBq p"      (bottom: two uprights, a "B"/"a"-like form, "q"; then a large clear "p" - if inverted, this would be a "d" and the group would read right-to-left as "d b..ll")
image-012 line 8: ]i(?) e(?) / o(?)[ / as seen: ". o"      (a small tick, then a large round "e"/"o")
image-012 line 9: ]il(?) i(?)[ / as seen: "l ı"      (two or three uprights at the bottom edge; cut)
(No word can be read in this tile.)

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
All twelve images were viewed. Two overviews (image-001 with scale;
image-007 without) and ten native tiles: 002-006 run down the strip of
image-001 with overlaps (002/003, 003/004, 004/005, 005/006 share one to two
lines each, noted above); 008-012 run down the strip of image-007 with
overlaps (008/009, 009/010, 010/011 share one to two lines each; 011/012
share only a blank gap). I attempted every visible line. Because only c. 1 cm
of width is exposed, NO connected span of ten lines of text exists in the
ordinary sense; what exists is a vertical run of 3-8 letter slices from
